notes.decision: The lines bracketing the chapter title with ⲛⲏ are likely scribal ornaments / decorative dividers rather than meaningful text. Some editors interpret them as the demonstrative 'these,' but their position framing the chapter title supports an ornamental reading. Preserved untranslated.

Chapter title: 'The Four Powers of Those Who Grieve.' ⲧϥⲧⲟⲉ = 'the four' (ϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ); ⲛⲟ̄ⲁⲙ = plural of ⲟ̄ⲁⲙ/ϫⲟⲙ 'power'; ⲣ̄-ⲗⲩⲧⲏ = Greek λυπεῖν 'grieve, sorrow.' The chapter enumerates four cosmic-divine powers in grief: 1st = Mother of the Living One, 2nd = First Man, and (continuing on next page) two more.
ⲡⲏⲱ likely qualitative of ⲡⲱⲱⲛⲉ 'incline, turn' or related stem; with ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ 'of heart' = 'inclined-of-heart' = grieved/moved-in-heart. Translated 'inclined of heart.' Alternative: 'poured-of-heart.'

ⲙⲙⲟ = Lyc. for ⲙⲁⲁⲩ 'mother'; ⲡⲧⲱⲛϩ̄ likely 'the Living One' (Lyc. for ⲡⲱⲛϩ̄/ⲉⲧⲟⲛϩ̄). 'The Mother of the Living One' is the standard Manichaean Mother of Life (Mater Vivens). She is the First Grieving Power.
Idiom ⲭⲓ + ϣⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ 'take pity, have compassion' (= Sah. ϫⲓ-ϣⲉⲛϩⲧⲏϥ̄). The Mother of Life takes pity on her children = the imprisoned light-souls.

Reading uncertain. ⲛ̄ⲥⲱⲩ = 'after them' (idiom of yearning); ⲛ̄ⲓ̈ⲉⲧⲥ̄ unclear — possibly 'her own' (intensive ⲉⲣⲱ⸗) or related to ⲉⲓⲧⲥ̄/ⲏⲧⲥ̄ in some compound sense. Left as tentative 'with longing for them.'

Read as ⲥⲁⲧⲡ̄ 'chosen, elect' (qualitative). The doubled -ⲧⲧ is Lycopolitan orthography. Translated 'chosen one' rather than as a proper noun (the epithet of Zarathustra in earlier kephalaia is contextually inappropriate here).
ⲕⲁⲍ = Lyc. ϩⲓⲥⲉ/ⲕⲁϩ 'suffer, be afflicted'; with negation ⲧⲙ̄- and dative -ⲛⲉⲩ. The clause expresses the protective concern of the five sons for those pleasing to them.

Translated as 'bondages' tentatively; the form may relate to ⲥⲛⲁϩ 'bond, fetter' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲥⲛⲁϩ). The pairing with ⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ 'blows' supports an affliction/restraint sense. Could alternatively be 'sufferings/afflictions' more generally.

Mani identifies himself as the Third Grieving Power, connecting this passage to the kephalaion on the Four Powers Who Grieve (cf. accumulated vocabulary ⲣ̄-ⲗⲩⲧⲏ). The first was the Mother of the Living; the second is implied earlier (probably referenced in the discussion of the Five Sons in lines 1-7); Mani is the third; the fourth would be the firmaments' weeping.
ⲟⲩⲱⲍ = Lyc. ⲟⲩⲱϩ 'add, place upon'; ⲛⲍⲏⲧⲥ̄ 'in her' (referring to the Church). 'I added (set) within her the Mind of Light.'
Read as Lyc. reflex of ⲡⲟⲩϩⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'their joining'; ϩⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'be joined, agree.' The construction ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲍⲱⲧⲏ̄ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲉⲙ = 'they did not join themselves with the right hand'. Distinct from Greek ζώνη.
